# Product Requirements Document: 485

**Version:** 1.0.0  
**Created:** 2026-02-18

## 1. Overview

Project 485 requirements and specifications.

## 2. Objectives

- *Launch functional e-commerce platform** by Q2 2025
- *Migrate 50% of sales** from marketplaces to owned platform by Q4 2025
- *Build customer database** of 50,000 registered users in first year
- *Achieve profitability** on direct sales by Q3 2025
- generated content
- driven product recommendation engine
- Goals (Out of Scope for V1)
- International shipping (US-only initially)
- Subscription/membership programs
- Mobile native apps (mobile web only)

## 3. Success Metrics

- *Technical Readiness**:
- ✅ All 10 providers pass smoke tests
- ✅ End-to-end deployment successful on all providers
- ✅ Rollback tested and working
- ✅ Security audit passed
- ✅ Performance benchmarks met
- *Documentation Readiness**:
- ✅ API documentation 100% complete
- ✅ User guides for all providers
- ✅ Migration guide from AWS-only

### FR-1175: Consistency

Ensure all projects follow the same structure

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --

- Assisted Workflows

### FR-1177: Speed

Start with 80% of the structure already done

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### FR-1180: [PRD Documentation](../prd/README.md)

- Detailed PRD guidance

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --

- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams

- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management

- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |

- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml

- analysis project.yaml

- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management

- -------------|-----|-----|-------|

- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |

- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation

- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields

- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### FR-1187: Basic Initialization

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### FR-1190: Common Variables

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### FR-1194: Feature Comparison

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *Scale-ups**:

- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management

### FR-1197: Feature Comparison

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### FR-1200: Three-Point Estimation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline

- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"
- *Use placeholders for**:
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements
- --

- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"
- --

- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:

- 80 hours

- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements

- ✓ Common patterns across your projects

### FR-1204: Using PERT Template

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --

- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**

- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**

- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- --

- MM-DD"

### FR-1207: Template Variables Best Practices

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"
- *Use placeholders for**:
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- --

- MM-DD"
- --

- At least one goal
- At least one success metric

- *100% Rule**:

- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements

- ✓ Common patterns across your projects

- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines

- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6

- O) / 6]²

- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration

- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule

- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes

### FR-1214: Example 4: Using Multiple Templates

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --

- 01-15"

- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline

- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps

- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names

- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- --

- MM-DD"

- At least one goal

- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"

### FR-1217: 3. Scale Templates as Project Grows

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --
- *Create Your Document**
- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**
- 01-15"
- *Add Helpful Comments**
- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**
- When to use this template
- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"
- *Use placeholders for**:
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements
- --
- *Required Fields**:
- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"
- --
- *Required Sections**:
- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"
- id: "1.1"
- id: "1.2"
- *8/80 Rule** (Warning only):
- 80 hours
- *Dependency Validation**:
- *No Circular Dependencies**:
- *Validation Command**:
- *Valid Estimates**:
- *Reasonable Variance**:
- 3x optimistic
- *All Dependencies Exist**:
- *Validation Command**:
- --
- -project-name "Todo App" --template simple
- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --
- 01-01"
- 01-15"
- "v2.1: Added security review phase"
- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"
- --
- -verbose
- name}}
- i 's/{{project_name}}/My Project/g' my_file.md
- cache
- -template-path /path/to/template.yaml

### FR-1221: AI Generation Parameters

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### FR-1224: Template Inheritance

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- specific metadata

- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### FR-1231: Getting Help

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --

- 01-15"

- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"

### FR-1234: WBS Templates

- Work Breakdown Structures (YAML)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --

- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**

- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**

- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- --

- MM-DD"

- At least one goal

- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"

### FR-1241: Optimistic (O)

Best case if everything goes right

### FR-1242: Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions

### FR-1243: Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong

### FR-1244: > 90%

Very likely, low risk

### FR-1245: 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk

### FR-1246: 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk

### FR-1247: < 50%

Unlikely, high risk

### FR-1248: ES

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)

### FR-1249: EF

ES + Expected Duration

### FR-1250: LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project

### FR-1251: LS

LF - Expected Duration

### FR-1678: Optimistic (O)

Best case if everything goes right

### FR-1679: Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions

### FR-1680: Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong

### FR-1681: > 90%

Very likely, low risk

### FR-1682: 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk

### FR-1683: 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk

### FR-1684: < 50%

Unlikely, high risk

### FR-1685: ES

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)

### FR-1686: EF

ES + Expected Duration

### FR-1687: LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project

### FR-1688: LS

LF - Expected Duration

## 7. Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-1: Security notes

- Child processes are spawned with `shell: false` to avoid shell injection and quoting issues.
- Inputs are validated with Zod; unknown types are rejected.
- Avoid logging secrets; DEBUG only prints argv and minimal env context.

### NFR-2: Performance

- **Plan Generation:** <2 min for 2-3K lines (275x faster)
- **Execution:** 2.75x parallel speedup (91.7% efficiency)
- **Memory:** 75% reduction with batching
- **Overhead:** 3ms total (500x better than target)
- **Cost:** 99.95% cheaper than manual

---

### NFR-3: Performance Targets

| Metric | Target |
| :--- | :--- |
| Agent Startup | < 2ms |
| Human Startup | < 40ms |
| Input Latency | < 5ms (Asynchronous) |
| Completion UI | Instant (fzf-tab cached) |

- `started #TASK_ID`
- `wip #TASK_ID`

### 🟡 Total Work

Sum of PERT expected estimates for all leaf tasks

Linear progression from total work to zero

### 🟡 Actual Progress

Based on task completion status

### 🟡 Velocity

Work completed per day (hours/day)

### 🟡 Predicted Completion

Forecast based on current velocity

### 🟡 PV (Planned Value)

Budget × Planned % Complete (should have done)

### 🟡 EV (Earned Value)

Budget × Actual % Complete (actually done)

### 🟡 AC (Actual Cost)

Sum of actual costs (actually spent)

### 🟡 SV (Schedule Variance)

EV - PV

### 🟡 CV (Cost Variance)

EV - AC

### 🟡 SPI (Schedule Performance Index)

EV / PV

### 🟡 CPI (Cost Performance Index)

EV / AC

### 🟡 EAC (Estimate at Completion)

BAC / CPI

### 🟡 ETC (Estimate to Complete)

EAC - AC

### 🟡 VAC (Variance at Completion)

BAC - EAC

PV should reflect achievable targets

### 🟡 Track actual costs

More accurate AC = better forecasts

### 🟡 Review regularly

Weekly variance review catches issues early

### 🟡 Act on trends

Consistently low SPI/CPI requires intervention

### 🟡 Update forecasts

Adjust EAC when performance changes significantly

### 🟡 Review risks weekly

Risk status changes over time

### 🟡 Implement mitigations

Don't just identify, take action

### 🟡 Track to closure

Monitor risks until fully mitigated

### 🟡 Update probabilities

Adjust as project progresses

### 🟡 Add new risks

Continuously identify emerging risks

### 🟡 Share widely

Stakeholders need visibility

### 🟡 Update weekly

Fresh data drives better decisions

### 🟡 Follow up on actions

Recommendations only work if implemented

### 🟡 Track trends

Health declining over time is a warning sign

### 🟡 Be honest

Accurate reporting is better than optimistic reporting

### 🟡 Consistency

Ensure all projects follow the same structure

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- Assisted Workflows

- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards

- -template waterfall

- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables

- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"

- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields

- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

- O) / 6

- O) / 6]²

- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration

- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

### 🟡 Customization

Easy to adapt for your specific needs

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- Assisted Workflows

### 🟡 [PERT Documentation](../pert/README.md)

- PERT scheduling

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 Why Templates?

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**

- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration

- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata

- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- Assisted Workflows

- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### 🟡 Using Templates After Init

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 Manual Placeholder Replacement

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |

- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects

- ✗ Learning/experimentation

- O) / 6]²

### 🟡 Template Selection Guide

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml

### 🟡 What is PERT?

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 Example Calculation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata

- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- *100% Rule**:

- -project-name "Todo App" --template simple
- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- Assisted Workflows

- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
