```
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml

- analysis project.yaml

- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |

- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- Includes phase gate criteria

- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"

- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### FR-1139: Manual Placeholder Replacement

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --

- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**

- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**

- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements
- --

- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"
- --

- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)

- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"

- 80 hours

- *Validation Command**:

- 3x optimistic

### FR-1142: When to Use Each Template

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates

### FR-1146: What is PERT?

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01

- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --

- Assisted Workflows

- Success metrics from industry standards

- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables

- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### FR-1149: Example Calculation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- specific metadata

### FR-1152: Steps to Create a Custom Template

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --
- *Create Your Document**
- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**
- 01-15"
- *Add Helpful Comments**
- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**
- When to use this template
- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"
- *Use placeholders for**:
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements
- --
- *Required Fields**:
- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"
- --
- *Required Sections**:
- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"
- id: "1.1"
- id: "1.2"
- *8/80 Rule** (Warning only):
- 80 hours
- *Dependency Validation**:
- *No Circular Dependencies**:
- *Validation Command**:
- *Valid Estimates**:
- *Reasonable Variance**:
- 3x optimistic
- *All Dependencies Exist**:
- *Validation Command**:
- --
- -project-name "Todo App" --template simple
- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --
- 01-01"
- 01-15"
- "v2.1: Added security review phase"
- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"
- --
- -verbose
- name}}
- i 's/{{project_name}}/My Project/g' my_file.md
- cache
- -template-path /path/to/template.yaml

### FR-1156: WBS Validation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### FR-1159: Example 2: Agile Sprint Planning

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata

- ✓ Project/service names

- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --

- 01-15"

- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"

### FR-1166: 5. When to Customize Templates

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --
- *Create Your Document**
- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**
- 01-15"
- *Add Helpful Comments**
- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**
- When to use this template
- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"
- *Use placeholders for**:
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements
- --
- *Required Fields**:
- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"
- --
- *Required Sections**:
- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"
- id: "1.1"
- id: "1.2"
- *8/80 Rule** (Warning only):
- 80 hours
- *Dependency Validation**:
- *No Circular Dependencies**:
- *Validation Command**:
- *Valid Estimates**:
- *Reasonable Variance**:
- 3x optimistic
- *All Dependencies Exist**:
- *Validation Command**:

### FR-1169: Validation After AI Generation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration

- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates

- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- MM-DD"

- At least one goal

- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"

- 80 hours

- *Validation Command**:

- -project-name "Todo App" --template simple
- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --

- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"

### FR-1173: Template Libraries

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### FR-1176: Placeholder Not Replaced

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml

- analysis project.yaml

- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml

```

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed

- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints

- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01

```
**Acceptance Criteria:**

- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints

- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points

- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
```

```
### FR-1188: Optimistic (O)

Best case if everything goes right

### FR-1189: Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions

### FR-1190: Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong

### FR-1191: > 90%

Very likely, low risk

### FR-1192: 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk

### FR-1193: 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk

### FR-1194: < 50%

Unlikely, high risk

### FR-1195: ES

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)

### FR-1196: EF

ES + Expected Duration

### FR-1197: LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project

### FR-1198: LS

LF - Expected Duration
```

```
## 7. Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-1: Performance

- **Plan Generation:** <2 min for 2-3K lines (275x faster)
- **Execution:** 2.75x parallel speedup (91.7% efficiency)
- **Memory:** 75% reduction with batching
- **Overhead:** 3ms total (500x better than target)
- **Cost:** 99.95% cheaper than manual

---

### NFR-2: Performance Targets

| Metric | Target |
| :--- | :--- |
| Agent Startup | < 2ms |
| Human Startup | < 40ms |
| Input Latency | < 5ms (Asynchronous) |
| Completion UI | Instant (fzf-tab cached) |

### NFR-3: Performance Characteristics

### Complex Plan Benchmarks

**Sequential Execution**:
- Duration: ~21 hours
- CPU: 1 core
- Memory: 4GB
- Agents: 1 at a time

**Parallel Execution (15 agents)**:
- Duration: ~6 hours
- CPU: 16 cores
- Memory: 32GB
- Agents: 15 concurrent
- **Speedup: 3.5x**

**Cost Optimization**:
- Single pool (all GPT-4): $X
- N×M pools (mixed): $0.6X
- **Savings: 40%**

### 🔴 Severity:

CRITICAL

### 🟡 User Impact:

Runtime NameError when ty or zuban checks are enabled

### 🟡 Frequency:

Every execution with ty/zuban enabled

### 🟡 Workaround:

Disable ty/zuban with `--no-zuban` (but loses coverage)

### 🟠 Severity:

HIGH

### 🟡 User Impact:

Fixes applied by agents may introduce new ty/zuban issues that go undetected

### 🟡 Frequency:

Every parallel execution with re-scanning enabled

### 🟡 Example:

Agent fixes a ruff issue but breaks type annotations (ty would catch it but doesn't)

### 🟠 Severity:

HIGH

### 🟡 User Impact:

Agent overwhelm with 100+ file errors

### 🟡 Frequency:

Projects with 50+ files with errors

### 🟡 Severity:

MEDIUM

### 🟡 User Impact:

- Retry delays block all other retries in batch

### 🟡 Example:

- 10 tasks need retry with 4s backoff each

### 🟡 Severity:

MEDIUM

### 🟡 User Impact:

- File contention with 5-100 concurrent writers

### 🟡 Frequency:

All parallel executions

### 🟡 Severity:

MEDIUM

### 🟡 User Impact:

- False positive completions (agent claims success but file unchanged)

### 🟡 Frequency:

5-10% of tasks based on agent reliability

### 🟡 Severity:

MEDIUM

### 🟡 User Impact:

- Inflated error counts

### 🟡 Frequency:

20-30% of errors are duplicates across tools

### 🟡 Severity:

LOW-MEDIUM

### 🟡 User Impact:

- Multiple threads pick same agent simultaneously

### 🟡 Frequency:

1-5% of parallel executions with 20+ tasks

### 🟡 Severity:

MEDIUM

### 🟡 User Impact:

- False positives (marks failed tasks as complete)

### 🟡 Frequency:

2-5% of tasks misclassified
```

### 🟡 Monitoring

### 🔴 Non-blocking:

Other tasks continue while retries are scheduled

### 🟡 Concurrent:

Multiple retries can be waiting simultaneously

### 🟡 Efficient:

No thread blocked on `time.sleep()`

### 🔴 Scalable:

100 retries scheduled = O(1) threads vs O(100) with blocking

### 🟡 Zero Contention:

Each task writes to own file

### 🟡 Better Organization:

Logs organized by task

### 🟡 Parallel Safe:

No locking needed

### 🟡 Debugging:

Easy to find specific task logs

### 🟡 Performance:

No lock/unlock overhead

### 🟡 Deterministic:

Clear success/failure criteria

### 🟡 Confidence Scores:

Know how sure the system is

### 🟡 Extensible:

Easy to add new validation checks

### 🟡 Debuggable:

Structured data vs string matching

### 🟡 Future-proof:

Agents can return better data over time

### 🟡 Use clear naming

`authentication.md`, `user-management.md`

### 🟡 Keep specs focused

One spec per major feature/component

### 🟡 Version consistently

Use semantic versioning

### 🟡 Create GitHub Issues from WBS Tasks

Automatically create issues with proper metadata, labels, and estimates

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- -----------|--------------|--------------|
- *Mark as Completed:**
- `fixes #TASK_ID`
- `closes #TASK_ID`
- `resolves #TASK_ID`
- `completes #TASK_ID`
- *Mark as In Progress:**
- `in progress on #TASK_ID`
- `working on #TASK_ID`
- `started #TASK_ID`
- `wip #TASK_ID`
- *Examples:**
- m "fixes #1.1 - authentication working"
- m "in progress on #2.3 and #2.4"
- *Set Status:**
- *Set Progress:**
- -repo owner/repo`
- -repo owner/repo`
- create_issue: 2
- update_issue: 3
- Issue #123 has no task ID - cannot sync
- *Resolution:**
- *Task ID:** `1.1``
- run sync
- `wbs-task` - Identifies WBS-synchronized issues
- `status: *` - Task status labels
- `priority: *` - Priority labels
- if one fails, others continue.
- *Fix:** Set valid token in environment or `.env` file
- v
- GitHubClient operations
- WBSGitHubMapper bidirectional sync
- StatusTracker parsing
- Conflict detection
- Error handling
- plan_wbs_to_github() │
- plan_github_to_wbs() │
- execute_sync()       │
- create_issue()       │
- update_issue()       │
- get_wbs_issues()     │
- parse_commit()│
- parse_comment()│
- *Always run dry-run first**: Use `--dry-run` to preview changes
- *Sync regularly**: Run `sync pull` daily to catch GitHub updates
- *Use commit patterns**: Follow `fixes #TASK_ID` pattern for auto-tracking
- *Backup mappings**: Commit `github_mapping.json` to version control
- *Handle conflicts promptly**: Don't ignore conflict warnings
- *Check rate limits**: Monitor API usage for large repos
- *Problem:** Issue was created manually without task ID
- *Solution:** Add task ID to issue:
- Title: `[1.1] Task Name`
- Or body: `**Task ID:** `1.1``
- *Problem:** Issue references deleted task
- *Solution:** Either:
- add task to WBS
- *Problem:** `github_mapping.json` is invalid JSON
- *Solution:**
- sync all)

### 🟡 Consistency

Ensure all projects follow the same structure

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |

- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects

### 🟡 [PRD Documentation](../prd/README.md)

- Detailed PRD guidance

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"

- i 's/{{project_name}}/My Project/g' my_file.md

### 🟡 [Main Planning Guide](../README.md)

- Overall planning workflow

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --

- ✓ Sprint numbers

- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"

- 80 hours

- *Validation Command**:

- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows

- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards

- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### 🟡 Common Variables

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 Template Selection Guide

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --
- *Create Your Document**
- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**
- 01-15"
- *Add Helpful Comments**
- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**
- When to use this template
- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"
- *Use placeholders for**:
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements
- --
- *Required Fields**:
- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"
- --
- *Required Sections**:
- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"
- id: "1.1"
- id: "1.2"
- *8/80 Rule** (Warning only):
- 80 hours
- *Dependency Validation**:
- *No Circular Dependencies**:
- *Validation Command**:
- *Valid Estimates**:
- *Reasonable Variance**:
- 3x optimistic
- *All Dependencies Exist**:
- *Validation Command**:
- --
- -project-name "Todo App" --template simple
- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --
- 01-01"
- 01-15"
- "v2.1: Added security review phase"
- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"
- --
- -verbose
- name}}
- i 's/{{project_name}}/My Project/g' my_file.md
- cache
- -template-path /path/to/template.yaml

### 🟡 Feature Comparison

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 Three-Point Estimation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata

- ✓ Dates

- ✓ Sprint numbers

- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
