- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### 🟡 Template Variables Best Practices

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --

- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**

- *Add Helpful Comments**
- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**
- When to use this template
- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"
- *Use placeholders for**:
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements
- --
- *Required Fields**:
- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"
- --
- *Required Sections**:
- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"
- id: "1.1"
- id: "1.2"
- *8/80 Rule** (Warning only):
- 80 hours
- *Dependency Validation**:
- *No Circular Dependencies**:
- *Validation Command**:
- *Valid Estimates**:
- *Reasonable Variance**:
- 3x optimistic
- *All Dependencies Exist**:
- *Validation Command**:

### 🟡 PERT Validation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Company security baseline

- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

### 🟡 Example 4: Using Multiple Templates

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- -target-date 2025-03-01

- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- Assisted Workflows

- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks

- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### 🟡 3. Scale Templates as Project Grows

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 AI-Assisted Workflows

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |

- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |

- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

### 🟡 Template Inheritance

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Focus: Audit trail, risk management

- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |

### 🟡 WBS Templates

- Work Breakdown Structures (YAML)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- --

- MM-DD"
- --

- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"

- 80 hours

- *Validation Command**:

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates

- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation

- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- Assisted Workflows

- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"

- -from-prd my_project.md --ai

- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields

- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

### 🟡 Optimistic (O)

Best case if everything goes right

### 🟡 Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions

### 🟡 Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong

### 🟡 > 90%

Very likely, low risk

### 🟡 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk

### 🟡 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk

### 🟠 < 50%

Unlikely, high risk

### 🟡 ES

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)

### 🟡 EF

ES + Expected Duration

### 🟡 LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project

### 🟡 LS

LF - Expected Duration

- Low uncertainty: P = 1.5 × O

- Add contingency tasks

- Track actual vs. estimates

- Reduce critical path length

### 🟡 PERT Validation

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- `NonFunctionalRequirement`: Performance, security, etc.
- `Risk`: Risk assessment with mitigation
- `PRDData`: Complete PRD structure
- `WBSTask`: Individual work items
- `WBSPhase`: Major project phases
- `WBSData`: Complete work breakdown
- `PERTData`: Timeline and critical path analysis
- `AgentConfigData`: Multi-agent orchestration settings
- `PlanData`: Complete plan container

- Draft resume on restart
- Template loading
- Progress visualization

### 🟡 Error Handling

### 🟡 Custom Validators

Plugin system for domain rules

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- `NonFunctionalRequirement`: Performance, security, etc.
- `Risk`: Risk assessment with mitigation
- `PRDData`: Complete PRD structure
- `WBSTask`: Individual work items
- `WBSPhase`: Major project phases
- `WBSData`: Complete work breakdown
- `PERTData`: Timeline and critical path analysis
- `AgentConfigData`: Multi-agent orchestration settings
- `PlanData`: Complete plan container
- *Key Features**:
- Field validation with custom validators
- Cross-field validation (e.g., O ≤ M ≤ P estimates)
- Graph algorithms (circular dependency detection)
- Measurable metrics validation
- *Lines**: ~100
- *Purpose**: Auto-detect and parse multiple input formats
- `FormatDetector`: Auto-detect JSON/Markdown/Interactive
- `parse_json()`: Parse and validate JSON input
- `parse_markdown_section()`: Extract markdown sections
- `parse_markdown_list()`: Parse bullet/numbered lists
- *Supported Formats**:
- Interactive Q&A (default)
- JSON (structured data)
- Markdown (documents)
- *Lines**: ~600 (across 4 collectors)
- *Purpose**: Collect data for each phase
- Project metadata
- Goals with metrics
- Personas
- Functional requirements
- Non-functional requirements
- Risks and constraints
- Task hierarchy
- Estimates (O/M/P)
- Dependencies
- Resource assignments
- Requirements traceability
- Timeline estimation
- Critical path
- Risk factors
- Resource allocation
- Confidence intervals
- Parallelism settings
- Review gates
- Handoff points
- Integration configuration
- *Common Features**:
- Input method selection
- Example display
- Retry logic
- Validation feedback
- *Lines**: ~400
- *Purpose**: Orchestrate the planning process
- *Key Methods**:
- `run()`: Main interactive loop
- `collect_phase()`: Phase collection with retry
- `generate_plan_document()`: Create markdown output
- `save_plan()`: Persist to file
- `show_progress()`: Visual progress indicators
- `_save_draft()`: Auto-save functionality
- `_load_draft()`: Resume from draft
- *Features**:
- Phase navigation (forward/backward)
- Auto-save after each phase
- Draft resume on restart
- Template loading
- Progress visualization
- *Lines**: ~200
- *Purpose**: Command-line interface
- *Commands**:
- interactive`: Main planning workflow
- `--draft`: Resume from draft
- `--template`: Use template
- `--output`: Specify output file
- Checks schema compliance
- Shows validation errors
- Displays plan summary

### 🟡 8 BurndownChart tests

### 🟡 9 VarianceAnalyzer tests

### 🟡 6 RiskRegister tests

Risk identification, scoring, severity, prioritization, filtering, report generation

### 🟡 7 ProjectDashboard tests

Health calculation, progress, schedule, blockers, risks, dashboard generation, metrics export

### 🟡 12 Exporter tests

Full workflow, multi-format export

### 🟡 PV (Planned Value)

Budget × Planned %

### 🟡 EV (Earned Value)

Budget × Actual %

### 🟡 AC (Actual Cost)

Σ(actual_costs)

### 🟡 SV (Schedule Variance)

EV - PV

### 🟡 CV (Cost Variance)

EV - AC

### 🟡 SPI (Schedule Performance Index)

EV / PV

### 🟡 CPI (Cost Performance Index)

EV / AC

### 🟡 EAC (Estimate at Completion)

BAC / CPI

### 🟡 ETC (Estimate to Complete)

EAC - AC

### 🟡 VAC (Variance at Completion)

BAC - EAC

### 🟡 Type Safety

Full Pydantic validation

### 🟡 Error Handling

Graceful degradation when data missing

### 🟡 Documentation

Comprehensive docstrings

### 🟡 Testing

44 unit + integration tests

### 🟡 Clean Architecture

Separation of concerns

### 🟡 Extensibility

Easy to add new report types

### 🟡 Burndown

O(n) where n = number of tasks

### 🟡 Variance

O(n) for calculations, O(1) for metrics

### 🟡 Risk Register

O(n) for identification, O(n log n) for sorting

### 🟡 Dashboard

O(n) aggregates all components

### 🟡 PV (Planned Value)

Budget × Planned % Complete (should have done)

Sum of actual costs (actually spent)

EV - PV

EV - AC

EV / PV

### 🟡 CPI (Cost Performance Index)

EV / AC

### 🟡 EAC (Estimate at Completion)

BAC / CPI

### 🟡 ETC (Estimate to Complete)

EAC - AC

### 🟡 VAC (Variance at Completion)

BAC - EAC

## 9. Architecture Overview

Built on battle-tested libraries (not custom implementations):
- **Packaging:** pyproject.toml (PEP 517/518), hatchling
- **Configuration:** settings.yaml (Pydantic validation)
- **Secrets:** python-dotenv (multi-source)
- **CLI:** Typer + Rich + rich-click
- **TUI:** Textual (async)
- **GUI:** PyQt6 + QtCharts
- **Parsing:** python-frontmatter, mistune
- **AI:** Instructor, Pydantic AI, LangGraph
- **Execution:** graphlib (stdlib), NetworkX
- **Database:** SQLAlchemy 2.0
- **Messaging:** NATS, Redis

---

## 7. Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-1: CSE 535 A2 - MOBILE SECURITY (Post-Quantum Cryptography)

### Requirement 1: Parameter Selection

**What it means:**
- Choose secure n, q, σ for Learning with Errors problem
- Prevent known attacks: Gaussian elimination, BKZ lattice reduction
- Typical values: n=256-512, q=2^12-2^16, σ=√2-√8

**How we validate:**
```
Input: Security level (128, 192, 256-bit)
Output: (n, q, σ) parameters

Example:
  Security=128 bits → (n=256, q=2^13, σ=√2.7)
  Security=256 bits → (n=512, q=2^16, σ=√4.0)

Check:
- n is power of 2: ✓
- q is prime or 2^k: ✓
- σ provides c

  - [ ] Matrix-vector multiplication with modular arithmetic
  - [ ] Add error vector

  - [ ] Extract A, b from public key tuple
  - [ ] Sum selected rows based on binary vector
  - [ ] Add message * floor(p/2) contribution

## Test Cases

### Public Key Generation
```
A = np.array([[1, 6, 6, 2], [6, 0, 5, 3], [2, 5, 4, 1]])
s = np.array([3, 4, 0, 6])
e = np.array([0, -1, 1])
p = 7

b = generate_public_key_vector(A, s, e, p)
assert np.array_equal(b, np.array([4, 0, 5]))
```

### Encryption
```
public_key = (A, np.array([4, 0, 5]))
random_vector = np.array([1, 0, 1])

u0, v0 = encrypt(public_key, random_vector, 0, 7)
assert np.array_equal(u0, np.array([3, 4, 3, 3]))
assert v0 == 2

u1, v1 = encrypt(public_key, random_vector, 1, 7)
assert np.array_equal(u1, np.array([3, 4, 3, 3]))
assert v1 == 5
```

### Decryption
```
s = np.array([3, 4, 0, 6])

msg0 = decrypt(s, (np.array([3, 4, 3, 3]), 2), 7)
assert msg0 == 0

msg1 = decrypt(s, (np.array([3, 4, 3, 3]), 5), 7)
assert msg1 == 1
```

### Phase 12: CLI entry points without documentation of why each exists

**Pattern:**

Agent #2 creates: setup_python314_stable.py (11:48) - doesn't know about Agent #1's work
Agent #3 analyzes: "Which is correct?" Creates CLEANUP_LOG.md
```

- Oct 14 05:45 and 11:49: Test scripts 6+ hours apart suggest different agents

### Root Cause #3: Conservative File Creation Philosophy
**Frequency:** 5 instances
**Severity:** MEDIUM
**Examples:**
- Creating `atoms-mcp-enhanced.py` instead of modifying `atoms`
- Creating `setup_production_environment.py` instead of updating existing setup
- Creating new test files instead of extending existing ones

**Pattern:**
```
Agent calculates risk:
  ↓
"Modifying existing file might break things"
  ↓
"Creating new file is safer"
  ↓
"Let others decide which to use"
  ↓
Result: Parallel safe variants
```

**Evidence:** Both wrapper files (atoms_mcp_simplified.py and atoms-mcp-enhanced.py) call the SAME underlying function - evidence that agent knew how to parameterize but chose to create separate files instead.

---

### Root Cause #4: No Clear "Source of Truth" Architecture
**Frequency:** 7 instances
**Severity:** HIGH
**Examples:**
- Both setup approaches and tests coexist
- Multiple consolidation documents (code + markdown)
- Multiple phase status documents

**Pattern:**
```
Multiple valid ways to implement:
  ↓
No clear architecture decision documented
  ↓
Each agent creates their preferred variant
  ↓
Result: 3-5 parallel implementations
```

**Evidence:** ATOMS-PHENOMIGR.py duplicates CONSOLIDATION_ANALYSIS_AND_PLAN.md perfectly - both agents created "comprehensive migration plan" independently.

---

### Root Cause #5: Premature Documentation Variant Creation
**Frequency:** 4 instances
**Severity:** MEDIUM
**Examples:**
- CLEANUP_LOG.md documents cleanup (analysis)
- CLEANUP_SUMMARY.md documents same cleanup (summary)
- PHASE3_STATUS_SUMMARY.md + PHASE2_COMPLETE_SUMMARY.md (similar intent)

**Pattern:**
```
Agent completes analysis:
  ↓
Creates documentation of findings
  ↓
Different agent needs slightly different format
  ↓
Creates second documentation variant
  ↓
Result: Redundant docs with minimal difference
```

**Evidence:** CLEANUP_LOG.md is 280+ lines; if same info needed in summary format, agent could have created CLEANUP_SUMMARY as 50-line version with link to CLEANUP_LOG. Instead, created completely separate document.

**Evidence:**

- Shows they knew the pattern but didn't refactor atoms itself
- Both files are 15 lines with identical structure

**Impact:** Confusion about which entry point to use; maintenance burden if atoms.main() signature changes

# Product Requirements Document: zentest

**Version:** 1.0.0  
**Created:** 2026-02-18

## 1. Overview

Project zentest requirements and specifications.

## 2. Objectives

- Achievement Stats
- Personalization
- MacroProgressCard
- Goal Setting
- Weekly Progress Widget
- Business

## 3. Success Metrics

- *Performance Targets**
- **Scale**: Support 100,000+ concurrent agents
- **Latency**: < 100ms communication at full scale
- **Reliability**: 99.99% uptime SLA
- **Efficiency**: > 80% resource utilization
- **Fault Tolerance**: Handle 30% agent failures
- *Business Metrics**
- **Enterprise Adoption**: 50+ Fortune 500 customers
- **Developer Productivity**: 300% improvement in multi-agent development
- **Platform Revenue**: $100M+ ARR potential

## 4. Stakeholders

## 5. Target Users

- admin
- User
- user

## 6. Functional Requirements

### FR-1: MCP Registry Integration

Modified fork of the official [MCP Registry](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry) - users can now claim MCP servers with GitHub credentials

### FR-2: Completely Rewritten Discovery Process

Enhanced server detection and management with improved performance and reliability

### FR-3: Full Streamable HTTP Support

Complete implementation of Streamable HTTP transport protocol

### FR-4: OAuth for MCP Servers

OAuth authentication handled by plugged.in with state-of-the-art encryption - no client-side authentication needed anymore

### FR-5: Trending Servers with Analytics

Every MCP tool call via pluggedin-mcp is tracked and displayed in trending servers

### FR-6: Bidirectional Notifications

MCP proxy can now send, receive, mark as read, and delete notifications

### FR-7: Smart Server Wizard

Multi-step wizard with GitHub verification, environment detection, and registry submission

### FR-8: Enhanced Security

Comprehensive input validation with Zod schemas and XSS/SSRF protection

### FR-9: Multi-Workspace Support

Switch between different sets of MCP configurations to prevent context pollution

### FR-10: Interactive Playground

Test and experiment with your MCP tools directly in the browser

### FR-11: Tool Management

Discover, organize, and manage AI tools from multiple sources

### FR-12: Resource & Template Discovery

View available resources and resource templates for connected MCP servers

### FR-13: Custom Instructions

Add server-specific instructions that can be used as MCP prompts

### FR-14: Prompt Management

Discover and manage prompts from connected MCP servers

### FR-15: End-to-End Encryption

All sensitive MCP server configuration data (commands, arguments, environment variables, URLs) is now encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM

### FR-16: Per-Profile Encryption

Each profile has its own derived encryption key, ensuring complete isolation between workspaces

### FR-17: Secure Server Sharing

Shared servers use sanitized templates that don't expose sensitive credentials

### FR-18: Transparent Operation

Encryption and decryption happen automatically without affecting the user experience

### FR-19: AI-Generated Documents

MCP servers can create and manage documents in your library with full attribution

### FR-20: Document Preview Modal

View PDFs, images, and text files directly in the browser with zoom controls

### FR-21: Enhanced Document Viewer

Navigate between documents, fullscreen mode, and metadata display

### FR-22: Multi-Format Support

Native rendering for PDFs, images, markdown, and various code file formats

### FR-23: Model Attribution Tracking

Complete history of which AI models created or updated each document

### FR-24: Advanced Document Search

Semantic search with filtering by AI model, date, tags, and source type

### FR-25: Document Versioning

Track changes and maintain version history for AI-generated content

### FR-26: Multi-Source Support

Documents from uploads, AI generation, or API integrations

### FR-27: Document Library with RAG

Upload and manage documents that serve as knowledge context for AI interactions

### FR-28: Real-Time Notifications

Get instant notifications for MCP activities with optional email delivery

### FR-29: Progressive Server Initialization

Faster startup with resilient server connections

### FR-30: Enhanced Security

Industry-standard sanitization and secure environment variable handling

### FR-31: Improved UI/UX

Redesigned playground, better responsive design, and theme customization

### FR-32: Server Notes

Add custom notes to each configured MCP server

### FR-33: Extensive Logging

Detailed logging capabilities for MCP interactions in the Playground

### FR-34: Expanded Discovery

Search for MCP servers across GitHub, Smithery, and npmjs.com

### FR-35: Email Verification

Secure account registration with email verification

### FR-36: Self-Hostable

Run your own instance with full control over your data

### FR-37: Testing Infrastructure

Comprehensive test coverage for core functionality

### FR-38: Playground Optimizations

Improved performance for log handling

### FR-39: Embedded Chat (Phase 2)

Generate revenue through embeddable AI chat interfaces

### FR-40: AI Assistant Platform (Phase 3)

### FR-41: Privacy-Focused Infrastructure (Phase 4)

Dedicated RAG servers and distributed GPU services

### FR-43: Collaboration & Sharing

### FR-44: Full MCP Streamable HTTP Support

### FR-45: OAuth 2.1 Integration

### FR-46: Enhanced Configuration

Custom headers and session management for Streamable HTTP servers

### FR-47: Multi-Language Support

Updated translations for all supported languages

### FR-48: Document Library with RAG Integration

Upload and manage documents that enhance AI context

### FR-49: Real-Time Notification System

Get instant updates on MCP activities with email support

### FR-50: Progressive Server Initialization

Faster, more resilient MCP server connections

### FR-51: Enhanced Playground UI

Redesigned layout with better responsiveness and streaming indicators

### FR-52: Improved RAG Query Security

Replaced custom sanitization with `sanitize-html` library for robust XSS protection

### FR-53: Secure Environment Variable Parsing

Implemented `dotenv` library for proper handling of quotes, multiline values, and special characters

### FR-54: Enhanced Input Validation

Added comprehensive validation for all user inputs across the application

### FR-55: Strengthened API Security

Implemented rate limiting and improved authentication checks

### FR-56: Tools API (`/api/tools`)

Implements 5-minute throttling to avoid repeated discovery attempts

### FR-57: Discovery API (`/api/discover`)

Uses 2-minute throttling for explicit discovery requests

### FR-58: In-memory caching

Tracks recent discovery attempts to prevent duplicate calls

### FR-59: Failure recovery

Clears throttle cache on discovery failures to allow faster retries

### FR-60: Single query optimization

Fetches server data and tool counts in one query using LEFT JOIN

### FR-61: Reduced database load

Eliminates redundant tool count queries

### FR-62: Indexed lookups

Uses existing database indexes for faster server and tool queries

### FR-63: Asynchronous discovery

All discovery processes run in background without blocking API responses

### FR-64: Error handling

Comprehensive error handling with automatic retry mechanisms

### FR-65: Status tracking

Provides clear feedback on discovery progress and throttling status

### FR-66: Reduced API latency

Faster response times for tools API calls

### FR-67: Lower database load

Fewer redundant queries and optimized data fetching

### FR-68: Better user experience

Prevents duplicate work and provides instant feedback

### FR-69: Scalable architecture

Can handle multiple concurrent discovery requests efficiently

## 7. Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-1: 🔐 SECURITY & COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS

### **Security Framework**
- **Zero Trust Architecture**: Verify every agent interaction
- **End-to-End Encryption**: All communication encrypted in transit and at rest
- **Multi-Factor Authentication**: Required for all administrative access
- **Regular Security Audits**: Quarterly penetration testing
- **Vulnerability Management**: Automated scanning and remediation

### **Compliance Standards**
- **SOC2 Type II**: Security, availability, confidentiality controls
- **GDPR Compliance**: Europea

## 8. Features

### 🟡 MCP Registry Integration

Modified fork of the official [MCP Registry](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry) - users can now claim MCP servers with GitHub credentials

### 🟡 Completely Rewritten Discovery Process

Enhanced server detection and management with improved performance and reliability

### 🟡 Full Streamable HTTP Support

Complete implementation of Streamable HTTP transport protocol

### 🟡 OAuth for MCP Servers

OAuth authentication handled by plugged.in with state-of-the-art encryption - no client-side authentication needed anymore

### 🟡 Trending Servers with Analytics

Every MCP tool call via pluggedin-mcp is tracked and displayed in trending servers

### 🟡 Bidirectional Notifications

MCP proxy can now send, receive, mark as read, and delete notifications

### 🟡 Smart Server Wizard

Multi-step wizard with GitHub verification, environment detection, and registry submission

### 🟡 Enhanced Security

Comprehensive input validation with Zod schemas and XSS/SSRF protection

### 🟡 Multi-Workspace Support

Switch between different sets of MCP configurations to prevent context pollution

### 🟡 Interactive Playground

Test and experiment with your MCP tools directly in the browser

### 🟡 Tool Management

### 🟡 Resource & Template Discovery

### 🟡 Custom Instructions

### 🟡 Prompt Management

Discover and manage prompts from connected MCP servers

### 🟡 End-to-End Encryption

All sensitive MCP server configuration data (commands, arguments, environment variables, URLs) is now encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM

Each profile has its own derived encryption key, ensuring complete isolation between workspaces

### 🟡 Secure Server Sharing

Shared servers use sanitized templates that don't expose sensitive credentials

### 🟡 Transparent Operation

Encryption and decryption happen automatically without affecting the user experience
